paragraphs: In Gwynedd the council's own fostering service is Foster Wales Gwynedd, known in Welsh as Maethu Cymru Gwynedd. Its team works from the Arfon area social services office at Penrallt in Caernarfon, and it is one of the 22 not-for-profit council fostering services that make up Foster Wales. Children across the county are looked after by its carers and by the services shown above.

The council says the children who need a family here can be toddlers, teenagers, young parents or brothers and sisters, and that local carers let children stay in their own community, near their friends and school. In November 2024 it said 170 of the more than 7,000 children in care across Wales were in Gwynedd, that the county had more than 71 fostering households, and that it needed at least 12 more carers so children could stay local. You can make your enquiry in Welsh or English.

Foster Wales Gwynedd publishes its payments. It describes a child's allowance of £229 to £261 a week depending on age, to cover food, clothes, toiletries and bills, and a carer's fee of £109 to £438 a week depending on experience, how long you have fostered and the type of fostering. There are extra payments for birthdays, religious festivals, mileage and equipment, up to 50% off council tax depending on the type of fostering, free parking in council car parks, and five days' extra leave for council staff who foster. Carers have a supervising social worker, support at any hour, training and mentoring.

In a Foster Wales survey reported by the council in May 2026, 93% of the carers who answered said they now felt confident responding to behaviour linked to trauma. Read our North Wales and Conwy pages for nearby areas, then talk to Foster Wales Gwynedd and one or two of the services above before you decide.
